candidate.title: scRNA-seq
candidate.scope: The assigned poster row labeled scRNA-seq / Single-cell mRNA sequencing, a single-cell poly(A)-primed mRNA-to-cDNA, PCR and shearing architecture associated by the listed citation with Tang et al. (2009). The matching collection page is headed scRNA-Seq: Single-Cell mRNA Sequencing and depicts the same route. This is the illustrated implementation within the broader single-cell RNA-sequencing family, not a claim that every family member has this preparation. The full image was inspected: CLASH above, SUPeR-seq below, the RNA Low-Level Detection heading and the partial chemical structure at the right are neighboring context, with no connecting arrows to the assigned row, and are not additional target methods. The endpoint is DNA; routine upstream isolation and downstream sequencing-library finishing are not expanded into unshown operations. Primary evidence for Tang is abstract-only; local preparation details are supported by the diagram and the secondary collection prose.

method_scopes.rationale: All five operations belong to the continuous, single scRNA-seq row. The initial yellow RNA icon is descriptive, the poly(T) symbol is a reagent addition, and the two strands at PCR are complementary DNA rather than independent branches. No pooling, split, integration, in situ sequencing or SUPeR-seq branch is connected to this route. The associated Tang abstract supports single-cell mRNA profiling, while the figure and matching secondary catalogue establish this schematic implementation. Broader scRNA-seq families are not asserted to use identical preparation.
